extraction.name: CADS: A Comprehensive Anatomical Dataset and Segmentation for Whole-Body Anatomy in Computed Tomography
extraction.description: CADS is an open-source framework for whole-body CT segmentation, providing a large-scale dataset of 22,022 CT volumes with full annotations for 167 anatomical structures.
extraction.creator: Murong Xu, Tamaz Amiranashvili, Femando Navarro, Maksym Fritsak, Ibrahim Ethem Hamamci, Suprosanna Shit, Bastian Wittmann, Sezgin Er, Sebastian M. Christ, Ezequiel de la Rosa, Julian Deseoe, Robert Graf, Hendrik Möller, Anjany Sekuboyina, Jan C. Peeken, Sven Becker, Giulia Baldini, Johannes Haubold, Felix Nensa, René Hosch, Nikhil Mirajkar, Saad Khalid, Stefan Zachow, Marc-André Weber, Georg Langs, Jakob Wasserthal, Mehmet Kemal Ozdemir, Andrey Fedorov, Ron Kikinis, Stephanie Tanadini-Lang, Jan S. Kirschke, and Stephanie E. Combs
extraction.publisher: University of Zurich, ETH Zurich, University Hospital Zurich, Technical University of Munich, and other institutions
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The CADS-dataset aggregates 22,022 CT volumes from 40 diverse sources, representing one of the most comprehensive repositories for medical image analysis to date.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Physical data collection, Document analysis, Software Collection, Web Scraping, Web API, Focus groups, Self-reporting, Customer feedback data, User-generated content data, Passive Data Collection
extraction.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: Only 4,695 (21%) of the initial collection contain partial annotations, while 79% lack any annotations.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: The collection spans more than 100 imaging facilities across 16 countries, capturing a wide spectrum of clinical variability.
extraction.rai:dataImputationProtocol: Automated annotation methodology grounded in pseudo-labeling, allowing use of images with no annotations, a single annotated structure, or multiple ones.
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Standardized preprocessing pipeline: reorient all images to the standard RAS convention, resample to a uniform 1.5 mm isotropic resolution, and simplify original affine transformation matrices.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Data preprocessing: reorient images to RAS convention, resample to 1.5 mm isotropic resolution, and simplify affine transformation matrices.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Pseudo-labeling strategy based on cluster assumption, using initial model predictions to assign labels to unlabeled samples.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Shape-informed label quality control: rank pseudo-labels in terms of likelihood estimation in shape space, and remove a certain percentage of worst pseudo-labels.
extraction.rai:annotatorDemographics: Three in-house medical research assistants and a radiation oncologist contribute additional manual annotations.
extraction.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: Versioning information: updating timeframe, maintainers, and deprecation policies are not explicitly stated.
extraction.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: Patient data, including facial features anonymized
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: Advancing robust AI solutions in radiology, making comprehensive anatomical analysis accessible to clinicians and researchers.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: Potential biases in data, including class imbalance and limited generalizability across institutions, populations, and imaging protocols.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Known limitations: limited anatomical coverage, insufficient data diversity, inconsistent annotation quality, human-dependent workflows, inadequate validation, limited availability, and accessibility barriers.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Dataset use cases: training, testing, validation, and fine-tuning of whole-body CT segmentation models.
